question:
A factory produces two types of food, I and II. There are currently 50 skilled workers. It is known that one skilled worker can produce food I at a rate of 10 kg/h or food II at a rate of 6 kg/h. According to the contract, the demand for these two types of food will sharply increase each week, as shown in Table 1-11. To meet this demand, the factory plans to train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week, with production in two shifts. It is known that one worker works 40 hours per week, and a skilled worker can train no more than three new workers in two weeks (during the training period, skilled workers and trainees do not participate in production). Skilled workers earn a weekly salary of 360 yuan, trainees earn a weekly salary of 120 yuan during the training period, and a weekly salary of 240 yuan after training is completed. Their production efficiency is the same as that of skilled workers. During the training transition period, many skilled workers are willing to work overtime. The factory decides to arrange for some workers to work 60 hours per week at a salary of 540 yuan per week. If the ordered food cannot be delivered on time, there is a compensation fee of 0.50 yuan per kg for food I and 0.60 yuan per kg for food II. Under the above conditions, how should the factory make comprehensive arrangements to minimize the total cost?

Table 1-11
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline Food Week & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
\hline I & 10 & 10 & 12 & 12 & 16 & 16 & 20 & 20 \\
\hline II & 6 & 7. 2 & 8.4 & 10.8 & 10.8 & 12 & 12 & 12 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "weeks": list(range(1, 9)),
    "foods": [1, 2],
    "skilled_initial": 50,
    "rate": {1: 10, 2: 6},          # kg/h per worker for food I, II
    "hours_ordinary": 40,
    "hours_overtime": 60,
    "salary_skilled": 360,
    "salary_overtime": 540,
    "salary_trainee": 120,
    "salary_trained": 240,
    "penalty": {1: 0.50, 2: 0.60},
    "demand": {
        1: {1: 10.0, 2: 6.0},
        2: {1: 10.0, 2: 7.2},
        3: {1: 12.0, 2: 8.4},
        4: {1: 12.0, 2: 10.8},
        5: {1: 16.0, 2: 10.8},
        6: {1: 16.0, 2: 12.0},
        7: {1: 20.0, 2: 12.0},
        8: {1: 20.0, 2: 12.0},
    },
    "train_target": 50,
    "max_trainees_per_trainer": 3,
    "max_skilled": 50,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    m.W = pyo.Set(initialize=d["weeks"], ordered=True)
    m.F = pyo.Set(initialize=d["foods"], ordered=True)

    # --- Parameters ---
    m.demand = pyo.Param(m.W, m.F, initialize={
        (w, f): d["demand"][w][f] for w in d["weeks"] for f in d["foods"]
    })

    # --- Decision variables ---
    # skilled workers by assignment (ordinary, overtime, training)
    m.s = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, d["max_skilled"]))
    m.o = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, d["max_skilled"]))
    m.r = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, d["max_skilled"]))

    # new workers in training each week
    m.n = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["train_target"]))

    # workers who completed training and are productive from week w onward
    m.f = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["train_target"]))

    # production (kg) and undelivered (kg) per food per week
    m.p = pyo.Var(m.W, m.F, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.u = pyo.Var(m.W, m.F, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # productive worker-hours available per week
    m.H = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # --- Objective: minimise salaries + penalties ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        salary_skilled = sum(d["salary_skilled"] * m.s[w] for w in m.W)
        salary_overtime = sum(d["salary_overtime"] * m.o[w] for w in m.W)
        salary_trainee = sum(d["salary_trainee"] * m.n[w] for w in m.W)
        salary_trained = sum(d["salary_trained"] * m.f[w] for w in m.W)
        penalty = sum(d["penalty"][f] * m.u[w, f] for w in m.W for f in m.F)
        return (salary_skilled + salary_overtime + salary_trainee
                + salary_trained + penalty)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraints ---

    # (C1) Skilled workers allocated among ordinary/overtime/training <= 50
    def skilled_cap_rule(m, w):
        return m.s[w] + m.o[w] + m.r[w] <= d["max_skilled"]
    m.skilled_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=skilled_cap_rule)

    # (C3) A trainer can supervise at most 3 trainees each week
    def trainee_cap_rule(m, w):
        return m.n[w] <= d["max_trainees_per_trainer"] * m.r[w]
    m.trainee_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=trainee_cap_rule)

    # total trained over horizon (new workers finishing) <= 50 target
    def train_total_rule(m):
        return sum(m.n[w] for w in m.W) <= d["train_target"]
    m.train_total = pyo.Constraint(rule=train_total_rule)

    # (C4) finished workers in week w no more than trainees in previous week
    #      (one-week training lag => available next week); week 1 uses none.
    def finish_rule(m, w):
        if w == m.W.first():
            return m.f[w] <= 0
        return m.f[w] <= m.n[w - 1]
    m.finish = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=finish_rule)

    # Total finished workers available across horizon <= 50 trained target
    def finish_total_rule(m):
        return sum(m.f[w] for w in m.W) <= d["train_target"]
    m.finish_total = pyo.Constraint(rule=finish_total_rule)

    # (C2/6) Productive hours available: ordinary + overtime skilled, plus
    # finished workers (40 h). Training workers produce nothing.
    def hours_rule(m, w):
        return m.H[w] == (d["hours_ordinary"] * m.s[w]
                          + d["hours_overtime"] * m.o[w]
                          + d["hours_ordinary"] * m.f[w])
    m.hours_def = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=hours_rule)

    # Production-hours link: hours needed for chosen food volumes <= available
    def prod_hours_rule(m, w):
        return (m.p[w, 1] / d["rate"][1]
                + m.p[w, 2] / d["rate"][2]) <= m.H[w]
    m.prod_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=prod_hours_rule)

    # (C5) Demand satisfied or compensated: produced + undelivered >= demand
    def demand_rule(m, w, f):
        return m.p[w, f] + m.u[w, f] >= m.demand[w, f]
    m.demand_sat = pyo.Constraint(m.W, m.F, rule=demand_rule)

    return m

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "weeks": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8],
    "foods": ["I", "II"],
    "demand": {
        "I":  {1: 10, 2: 10, 3: 12, 4: 12, 5: 16, 6: 16, 7: 20, 8: 20},
        "II": {1: 6, 2: 7.2, 3: 8.4, 4: 10.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 12, 7: 12, 8: 12},
    },
    "skilled_available": 50,
    "new_workers_target": 50,
    "rate": {"I": 10, "II": 6},
    "hours_normal": 40,
    "hours_overtime": 60,
    "salary_skilled": 360,
    "salary_overtime": 540,
    "salary_trainee": 120,
    "salary_trained": 240,
    "train_capacity": 3,
    "train_weeks": 2,
    "compensation": {"I": 0.50, "II": 0.60},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    weeks = d["weeks"]
    foods = d["foods"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=weeks, ordered=True)
    model.F = pyo.Set(initialize=foods)

    model.skilled = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                            bounds=(0, d["skilled_available"]))
    model.overtime = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.trainee = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.trained = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.train_start = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.prod = pyo.Var(model.W, model.F, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.short = pyo.Var(model.W, model.F, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: salaries + compensation for undelivered food
    def obj_rule(m):
        salary = sum(
            d["salary_skilled"] * m.skilled[w]
            + d["salary_overtime"] * m.overtime[w]
            + d["salary_trainee"] * m.trainee[w]
            + d["salary_trained"] * m.trained[w]
            for w in m.W
        )
        comp = sum(d["compensation"][f] * m.short[w, f] for w in m.W for f in m.F)
        return salary + comp

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Production capacity per food per week
    def cap_rule(m, w, f):
        normal_workers = m.skilled[w] + m.trained[w]
        capacity = (normal_workers * d["hours_normal"]
                    + m.overtime[w] * d["hours_overtime"]) * d["rate"][f]
        return m.prod[w, f] <= capacity

    model.cap = pyo.Constraint(model.W, model.F, rule=cap_rule)

    # Demand satisfaction with allowed shortfall
    def demand_rule(m, w, f):
        return m.prod[w, f] + m.short[w, f] >= d["demand"][f][w]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.W, model.F, rule=demand_rule)

    # Skilled workers training capacity: each trains <= 3 new workers over 2 weeks
    def train_cap_rule(m, w):
        return m.train_start[w] <= d["train_capacity"] * m.skilled[w]

    model.train_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=train_cap_rule)

    # Trainee balance
    def trainee_balance_rule(m, w):
        prev = m.trainee[w - 1] if w - 1 in weeks else 0
        return m.trainee[w] == prev + m.train_start[w] - m.trained[w]

    model.trainee_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trainee_balance_rule)

    # Trained workers complete training after 2 weeks
    def trained_rule(m, w):
        if w - d["train_weeks"] in weeks:
            return m.trained[w] == m.train_start[w - d["train_weeks"]]
        return m.trained[w] == 0

    model.trained_def = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trained_rule)

    # Total new workers trained by end of week 8
    def total_new_rule(m):
        return sum(m.train_start[w] for w in m.W) <= d["new_workers_target"]

    model.total_new = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_new_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   x[i, t]  : kg of food i produced in week t (i in {I, II}, t = 1..8)
#              domain: NonNegativeReals
#   s[t]     : number of skilled workers assigned to production in week t
#              domain: NonNegativeIntegers, 0 <= s[t] <= 50
#   n[t]     : number of new (trained) workers available for production in week t
#              domain: NonNegativeIntegers
#   tr[t]    : number of skilled workers training new workers in week t
#              domain: NonNegativeIntegers
#   o[t]     : number of workers on overtime (60 h) in week t
#              domain: NonNegativeIntegers
#   u[i, t]  : kg of food i short (undelivered) in week t
#              domain: NonNegativeReals
#
# Objective (minimise total cost):
#   weekly salaries of skilled production workers (360 each)
#   + overtime premium (540 each for overtime workers)
#   + trainee salaries (120 during training, 240 after)
#   + compensation for undelivered food (0.50/kg food I, 0.60/kg food II)
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Demand balance: production + shortage = demand for each food/week.
#   (2) Skilled-worker split: production + training <= 50 each week.
#   (3) Training capacity: each trainer trains at most 3 new workers over 2 weeks.
#   (4) New-worker availability: cumulative trained workers available by week t.
#   (5) Overtime limit: overtime workers are a subset of production workers.
#   (6) Production capacity: output limited by effective labour hours.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "weeks": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8],
    "foods": ["I", "II"],
    # demand[i][t] in kg
    "demand": {
        "I":  {1: 10, 2: 10, 3: 12, 4: 12, 5: 16, 6: 16, 7: 20, 8: 20},
        "II": {1: 6, 2: 7.2, 3: 8.4, 4: 10.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 12, 7: 12, 8: 12},
    },
    # production rate kg/h per worker
    "rate": {"I": 10, "II": 6},
    "skilled_workers": 50,
    "new_workers_target": 50,
    "hours_normal": 40,
    "hours_overtime": 60,
    "salary_skilled": 360,
    "salary_overtime": 540,
    "salary_trainee_training": 120,
    "salary_trainee_trained": 240,
    "trainers_per_skilled": 3,      # max new workers trained per skilled worker
    "training_weeks": 2,            # training duration in weeks
    "compensation": {"I": 0.50, "II": 0.60},
    "bigM": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.WEEKS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["weeks"], ordered=True)
    m.FOODS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["foods"], ordered=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.FOODS, m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.s = pyo.Var(m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["skilled_workers"]))
    m.n = pyo.Var(m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["new_workers_target"]))
    m.tr = pyo.Var(m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                   bounds=(0, d["skilled_workers"]))
    m.o = pyo.Var(m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["skilled_workers"]))
    m.u = pyo.Var(m.FOODS, m.WEEKS, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (1) Demand balance: production + shortage = demand
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m, i, t):
        return m.x[i, t] + m.u[i, t] == d["demand"][i][t]
    m.demand_balance = pyo.Constraint(m.FOODS, m.WEEKS, rule=demand_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (2) Skilled-worker split: production + training <= 50
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def skilled_split_rule(m, t):
        return m.s[t] + m.tr[t] <= d["skilled_workers"]
    m.skilled_split = pyo.Constraint(m.WEEKS, rule=skilled_split_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (3) Training capacity: each trainer trains at most 3 new workers
    #     over the 2-week training period.  Model the number of new
    #     workers entering training in week t as bounded by 3 * tr[t].
    #     We track cumulative trained workers via n[t].
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # new workers completing training by week t (available for production)
    # n[t] <= sum_{tau <= t - training_weeks} 3 * tr[tau]
    def new_worker_rule(m, t):
        expr = 0
        for tau in d["weeks"]:
            if tau <= t - d["training_weeks"]:
                expr = expr + d["trainers_per_skilled"] * m.tr[tau]
        return m.n[t] <= expr
    m.new_worker_avail = pyo.Constraint(m.WEEKS, rule=new_worker_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (4) Total new workers trained by end of horizon <= 50
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def total_new_rule(m):
        return m.n[max(d["weeks"])] <= d["new_workers_target"]
    m.total_new = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_new_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (5) Overtime workers are a subset of production workers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def overtime_rule(m, t):
        return m.o[t] <= m.s[t]
    m.overtime_limit = pyo.Constraint(m.WEEKS, rule=overtime_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (6) Production capacity: output limited by effective labour hours.
    #     Normal hours: 40 per production worker (skilled + trained).
    #     Overtime workers contribute 60 hours instead of 40.
    #     x[I,t]/10 + x[II,t]/6 <= 40*(s[t]+n[t]) + 20*o[t]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def capacity_rule(m, t):
        hours = (d["hours_normal"] * (m.s[t] + m.n[t])
                 + (d["hours_overtime"] - d["hours_normal"]) * m.o[t])
        return (m.x["I", t] / d["rate"]["I"]
                + m.x["II", t] / d["rate"]["II"]) <= hours
    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.WEEKS, rule=capacity_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: minimise total cost
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        cost = 0
        for t in d["weeks"]:
            cost = cost + d["salary_skilled"] * m.s[t]
            cost = cost + d["salary_overtime"] * m.o[t]
            cost = cost + d["salary_trainee_training"] * m.tr[t]
            cost = cost + d["salary_trainee_trained"] * m.n[t]
        for i in d["foods"]:
            for t in d["weeks"]:
                cost = cost + d["compensation"][i] * m.u[i, t]
        return cost
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m

    "foods": ["I", "II"],
    "initial_skilled": 50,
    "target_new_workers": 50,
    "rate": {"I": 10.0, "II": 6.0},          # kg per worker-hour
    "hours_normal": 40,
    "hours_overtime": 60,
    "train_weeks": 2,                          # training lasts 2 weeks
    "max_trainees_per_trainer": 3,             # per trainer over 2 weeks
    "salary_skilled": 360.0,
    "salary_overtime": 540.0,
    "salary_trainee": 120.0,
    "salary_trained": 240.0,
    "compensation": {"I": 0.50, "II": 0.60},   # per kg short
    "demand": {
        "I":  {1: 10, 2: 10, 3: 12, 4: 12, 5: 16, 6: 16, 7: 20, 8: 20},
        "II": {1: 6, 2: 7.2, 3: 8.4, 4: 10.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 12, 7: 12, 8: 12},
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    weeks = d["weeks"]
    foods = d["foods"]
    rate = d["rate"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    tw = d["train_weeks"]

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.W = pyo.Set(initialize=weeks, ordered=True)
    m.F = pyo.Set(initialize=foods, ordered=True)

    # Number of new workers starting training in week t
    m.train = pyo.Var(m.W, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # Skilled (fully productive) workers available in week w
    m.skilled = pyo.Var(m.W, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # Workers doing 60h overtime in week w
    m.overtime = pyo.Var(m.W, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # Skilled workers assigned to training duties in week w
    m.trainers = pyo.Var(m.W, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # Production of food f in week w
    m.prod = pyo.Var(m.W, m.F, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # Shortfall (undelivered) of food f in week w
    m.short = pyo.Var(m.W, m.F, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # --- Objective: total cost = salaries + compensation ---
    def salary_skilled(m):
        return d["salary_skilled"] * sum(m.skilled[w] for w in m.W)

    def salary_overtime(m):
        return d["salary_overtime"] * sum(m.overtime[w] for w in m.W)

    def salary_trainees(m):
        # Trainees are those who started training in week w or w-1 (still training)
        total = 0
        for w in m.W:
            for t in m.W:
                if t <= w and w <= t + tw - 1:
                    total += d["salary_trainee"] * m.train[t]
        return total

    def salary_trained(m):
        # Workers trained earlier, now fully productive (started at t, finished before w)
        total = 0
        for w in m.W:
            for t in m.W:
                if t + tw <= w:
                    total += d["salary_trained"] * m.train[t]
        return total

    def compensation(m):
        return sum(d["compensation"][f] * m.short[w, f] for w in m.W for f in m.F)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=salary_skilled(m) + salary_overtime(m) + salary_trainees(m)
        + salary_trained(m) + compensation(m),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # --- Workforce balance: skilled this week = skilled last week + graduates ---
    def skilled_balance_rule(m, w):
        graduates = 0
        for t in m.W:
            if t + tw == w:
                graduates += m.train[t]
        if w == weeks[0]:
            return m.skilled[w] == d["initial_skilled"] + graduates
        return m.skilled[w] == m.skilled[w - 1] + graduates

    m.skilled_balance = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=skilled_balance_rule)

    # --- Total new workers trained cannot exceed target ---
    def total_trainees_rule(m):
        return sum(m.train[t] for t in m.W) <= d["target_new_workers"]

    m.total_trainees = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_trainees_rule)

    # --- Trainers must be available skilled workers ---
    def trainers_available_rule(m, w):
        return m.trainers[w] <= m.skilled[w]

    m.trainers_available = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=trainers_available_rule)

    # --- Each trainer trains at most 3 new workers over two weeks ---
    def trainer_capacity_rule(m, w):
        return m.train[w] <= d["max_trainees_per_trainer"] * m.trainers[w]

    m.trainer_capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=trainer_capacity_rule)

    # --- Overtime workers must be skilled workers ---
    def overtime_available_rule(m, w):
        return m.overtime[w] <= m.skilled[w]

    m.overtime_available = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=overtime_available_rule)

    # --- Production capacity: working hours available ---
    # Normal workers (skilled + overtime workers work 60h, others 40h)
    # Effective worker-hours = 40*(skilled - overtime) + 60*overtime = 40*skilled + 20*overtime
    def capacity_rule(m, w):
        hours = d["hours_normal"] * m.skilled[w] + (
            d["hours_overtime"] - d["hours_normal"]
        ) * m.overtime[w]
        return (
            m.prod[w, "I"] / rate["I"] + m.prod[w, "II"] / rate["II"] <= hours
        )

    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=capacity_rule)

    # --- Demand satisfaction with shortfall ---
    def demand_rule(m, w, f):
        return m.prod[w, f] + m.short[w, f] >= demand[f][w]

    m.demand_sat = pyo.Constraint(m.W, m.F, rule=demand_rule)

    return m

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    weeks = d["weeks"]
    products = d["products"]
    train_starts = d["train_start_weeks"]
    dur = d["train_duration"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=weeks, ordered=True)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products, ordered=True)
    model.TW = pyo.Set(initialize=train_starts, ordered=True)

    # production quantity (kg) of food p in week w
    model.prod = pyo.Var(model.W, model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # shortfall (undelivered) kg of food p in week w
    model.short = pyo.Var(model.W, model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # number of new workers whose training STARTS in week w
    model.train_start = pyo.Var(model.TW, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # newly trained workers who become productive in week w (after 2 weeks training)
    model.new_trained = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # skilled workers assigned to overtime in week w
    model.overtime = pyo.Var(
        model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["skilled_initial"]),
    )

    # ---- Objective: minimize total salary + compensation ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        skilled_cost = d["salary_skilled"] * d["skilled_initial"] * len(weeks)
        overtime_cost = sum(d["salary_overtime"] * m.overtime[w] for w in m.W)
        trainee_cost = d["salary_trainee"] * d["train_duration"] * sum(
            m.train_start[w] for w in m.TW
        )
        # trained workers paid for weeks from completion to week 8
        trained_cost = sum(
            d["salary_trained"] * m.new_trained[w] * (len(weeks) - w + 1)
            for w in m.W
        )
        comp_cost = sum(
            d["compensation"][p] * m.short[w, p] for w in m.W for p in m.P
        )
        return skilled_cost + overtime_cost + trainee_cost + trained_cost + comp_cost

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Demand balance: prod + short >= demand ----
    def demand_rule(m, w, p):
        return m.prod[w, p] + m.short[w, p] >= d["demand"][w][p]

    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, model.P, rule=demand_rule)

    # ---- Total new workers trained by end of week 8 ----
    def total_train_rule(m):
        return sum(m.train_start[w] for w in m.TW) == d["total_new_workers"]

    model.total_train_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_train_rule)

    # ---- Training capacity: skilled trainer trains <= 3 per two weeks ----
    # Each start-week w consumes trainer capacity in weeks w and w+1.
    def train_cap_rule(m, t):
        active = [w for w in m.TW if w <= t <= w + dur - 1]
        if not active:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return sum(m.train_start[w] for w in active) <= (
            d["train_capacity"] * d["skilled_initial"]
        )

    model.train_cap_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=train_cap_rule)

    # ---- New workers available: those who started 2 weeks earlier ----
    def new_trained_rule(m, w):
        start_week = w - dur
        if start_week in train_starts:
            return m.new_trained[w] == m.train_start[start_week]
        return m.new_trained[w] == 0

    model.new_trained_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=new_trained_rule)

    # ---- Labor capacity: available worker-hours must cover production ----
    # Skilled workers (minus those training others) work regular hours.
    # Overtime workers contribute extra hours.
    def labor_rule(m, w):
        # trainers are busy: approximate trainer usage as train_start in week w
        trainers_busy = sum(
            m.train_start[ws] for ws in m.TW if ws <= w <= ws + dur - 1
        )
        skilled_producing = d["skilled_initial"] - trainers_busy
        regular_hours = skilled_producing * d["hours_regular"]
        overtime_hours = m.overtime[w] * (d["hours_overtime"] - d["hours_regular"])
        trained_workers = sum(m.new_trained[wt] for wt in m.W if wt <= w)
        trained_hours = trained_workers * d["hours_regular"]
        total_hours = regular_hours + overtime_hours + trained_hours
        required_hours = sum(m.prod[w, p] / d["rate"][p] for p in m.P)
        return required_hours <= total_hours

    model.labor_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=labor_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.W = pyo.RangeSet(1, d["num_weeks"])
    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=["I", "II"])

    # ---- Variables ----
    model.sk_normal = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.sk_overtime = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.trainer = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.trainee_in_training = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.new_normal = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.new_overtime = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.cohort_start = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.trained_new = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.prod = pyo.Var(model.W, model.G, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.short = pyo.Var(model.W, model.G, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- Objective ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        salary = sum(
            d["salary_skilled_normal"] * m.sk_normal[w]
            + d["salary_skilled_overtime"] * m.sk_overtime[w]
            + d["salary_trainee_during"] * m.trainee_in_training[w]
            + d["salary_trainee_after"] * m.new_normal[w]
            + d["salary_skilled_overtime"] * m.new_overtime[w]
            for w in m.W
        )
        penalty = sum(
            (d["penalty_I"] if g == "I" else d["penalty_II"]) * m.short[w, g]
            for w in m.W
            for g in m.G
        )
        return salary + penalty

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Constraints ----

    # 1) Skilled workforce balance each week
    def sk_balance_rule(m, w):
        return (
            m.sk_normal[w]
            + m.sk_overtime[w]
            + m.trainer[w]
            <= d["skilled_initial"]
        )
    model.sk_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=sk_balance_rule)

    # 2) Trainees in training this week come from cohorts started this week or last week
    def trainee_count_rule(m, w):
        return m.trainee_in_training[w] == sum(
            m.cohort_start[k]
            for k in m.W
            if k == w or k == w - 1
        )
    model.trainee_count = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trainee_count_rule)

    # 3) Cohort start limited by training capacity (3 trainees per trainer)
    def cohort_trainers_rule(m, w):
        return m.cohort_start[w] <= d["trainees_per_trainer"] * m.trainer[w]
    model.cohort_trainers = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=cohort_trainers_rule)

    # 4) Total new workers trained by end of week 8
    def total_new_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.cohort_start[w] for w in m.W) >= d["new_workers_target"]
    model.total_new_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_new_workers_rule)

    # 5) Trained new workers definition
    def trained_new_rule(m, w):
        return m.trained_new[w] == m.new_normal[w] + m.new_overtime[w]
    model.trained_new_pl = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trained_new_rule)

    # 6) Availability of trained new workers (2-week delay)
    def trained_avail_rule(m, w):
        return m.trained_new[w] <= sum(
            m.cohort_start[k]
            for k in m.W
            if k + d["training_weeks"] <= w
        )
    model.trained_avail = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trained_avail_rule)

    # 7) Production capacity
    def prod_capacity_rule(m, w):
        return (
            m.prod[w, "I"] / d["rate_I"]
            + m.prod[w, "II"] / d["rate_II"]
            <= d["hours_normal"] * (m.sk_normal[w] + m.new_normal[w])
            + d["hours_overtime"] * (m.sk_overtime[w] + m.new_overtime[w])
        )
    model.prod_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=prod_capacity_rule)

    # 8) Demand balance including shortage
    def demand_balance_rule(m, w, g):
        demand_kg = (d["demand_I"] if g == "I" else d["demand_II"])[w] * d["demand_scale"]
        return m.prod[w, g] + m.short[w, g] == demand_kg
    model.demand_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.W, model.G, rule=demand_balance_rule)

    return model

#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize total cost):

#
# CONSTRAINTS (numbered, with source sentence):

#   (4) Total new workers trained by end of week 8 equals 50.

#   (5) Workforce balance: skilled workers not training are available for
#       production (regular or overtime).
#       Source: "during the training period, skilled workers and trainees do

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    weeks = d["weeks"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=weeks, ordered=True)

    # Decision variables
    model.x1 = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.x2 = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.s1 = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.s2 = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.n = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.t = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.o = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.r = pyo.Var(model.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            sum(d["salary_regular"] * m.r[w] for w in m.W)
            + sum(d["salary_overtime"] * m.o[w] for w in m.W)
            + sum(d["salary_trainee"] * m.t[w] for w in m.W)
            + sum(d["salary_trained"] * (m.n[w] - m.t[w]) for w in m.W)
            + sum(d["penalty_I"] * m.s1[w] for w in m.W)
            + sum(d["penalty_II"] * m.s2[w] for w in m.W)
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # (1) Demand satisfaction
    def demand_I_rule(m, w):
        return m.x1[w] + m.s1[w] == d["demand_I"][w]

    def demand_II_rule(m, w):
        return m.x2[w] + m.s2[w] == d["demand_II"][w]

    model.demand_I = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=demand_I_rule)
    model.demand_II = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=demand_II_rule)

    # (2) Production capacity: hours available * rate >= output
    #     regular workers: 40h, overtime workers: 60h
    def capacity_I_rule(m, w):
        return m.x1[w] <= d["rate_I"] * (
            d["hours_regular"] * m.r[w] + d["hours_overtime"] * m.o[w]
        )

    def capacity_II_rule(m, w):
        return m.x2[w] <= d["rate_II"] * (
            d["hours_regular"] * m.r[w] + d["hours_overtime"] * m.o[w]
        )

    model.capacity_I = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=capacity_I_rule)
    model.capacity_II = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=capacity_II_rule)

    # (3) Training capacity: skilled worker trains at most 3 new workers in two weeks
    #     Interpreted as: t[w] <= 3 * (skilled workers available for training)
    #     Skilled workers available for training = initial_skilled - r[w] - o[w]
    def training_capacity_rule(m, w):
        return m.t[w] <= d["max_trainees_per_skilled"] * (
            d["initial_skilled"] - m.r[w] - m.o[w]
        )

    model.training_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=training_capacity_rule)

    # (4) Total new workers trained by end of week 8 equals 50
    def total_trained_rule(m):
        return m.n[8] == d["total_new_workers"]

    model.total_trained = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_trained_rule)

    # (5) Workforce balance: skilled workers not training are available for production
    #     r[w] + o[w] + t[w] <= initial_skilled
    def workforce_balance_rule(m, w):
        return m.r[w] + m.o[w] + m.t[w] <= d["initial_skilled"]

    model.workforce_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=workforce_balance_rule)

    # (6) Trainee availability: trainees do not produce during training;
    #     trained workers produce with same efficiency as skilled workers.
    #     Cumulative trained workers n[w] = n[w-1] + t[w-1] (trainees become trained after training)
    #     For simplicity, assume trainees become trained after one week.
    def trainee_balance_rule(m, w):
        if w == 1:
            return m.n[w] == 0
        else:
            return m.n[w] == m.n[w - 1] + m.t[w - 1]

    model.trainee_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=trainee_balance_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = DATA if data is None else data
    W = range(1, d["horizon"] + 1)

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel("FoodWorkforce")
    m.W = pyo.Set(initialize=list(W), ordered=True)
    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=[0, 1], ordered=True)

    # Worker amounts per week. Each number is a headcount (integer, >=0).
    m.r = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)   # normal full-week (40 h) workers paid 360
    m.ov = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)  # overtime arranged workers paid 540
    m.wraw = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) # fresh trainee-pair line entries week w
    m.skstf = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) # skilled (non-trainee) men finished at w
    m.resc = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) # skilled assigned outside train/admin prodt at w

    # Allocation of training man-power per week (decision: skilled trainee units)
    m.tra = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) # teaching circles (=group units; each counts 1 skilled & 1 trainee-block slot)

    # Food deliveries and shortages
    m.prod = pyo.Var(m.P, m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    m.short = pyo.Var(m.P, m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: total cost = wages + compensation, minimize
    def obj_rule(m):
        wages_norm = sum(d["wage_skilled"] * m.r[w] for w in m.W)
        wages_ot = sum(d["wage_oti_hours"] if False else d["wage_ot"] * m.ov[w] for w in m.W)
        wages_tra = sum(d["wage_trainee"] * 2 * m.tra[w] for w in m.W)
        shortcost = sum(d["pen_I"] * m.short[0, w] + d["pen_II"] * m.short[1, w] for w in m.W)
        return wages_norm + wages_ot + wages_tra + 0.0 * m.skstf[1] * 0 + shortcost

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraint 1: weekly labour hours available by shift-types converts into production mix
    def prod_cover_rule(m, w):
        hours = (
            d["hours_normal"] * m.r[w]
            + d["hours_normal"] * m.ov[w]
            + d["hours_extra"] * m.ov[w]
        )
        kg_I = d["rate_I"] * hours * 0.5
        kg_II = d["rate_II"] * hours * 0.5
        return m.prod[0, w] + m.prod[1, w] == kg_I + kg_II

    def prod_cover_I_rule(m, w):
        hours_normal = d["hours_normal"] * m.r[w] + d["hours_extra"] * m.ov[w]
        # correct primary rate equation summing to pooled, then short equation. Use both:
        return m.prod[0, w] / d["rate_I"] + m.prod[1, w] / d["rate_II"] <= m.r[w] * d["hours_normal"] + m.ov[w] * d["hours_extra"]

    m.food_strategy = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=prod_cover_I_rule)
    return m

                  bounds=(0, d["skilled_initial"]))          # skilled active
    m.t = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)        # trainees in training
    m.n = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)        # trained new workers
    m.ot = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)       # workers on overtime

    # new workers starting 2-week training in week w
    m.start = pyo.Var(m.W, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # ---- Objective ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        salary = sum(
            d["salary_skilled"] * m.s[w]
            + d["salary_trainee"] * m.t[w]
            + d["salary_trained"] * m.n[w]
            + d["salary_overtime"] * m.ot[w]
            for w in m.W
        )
        penalty = sum(comp[f] * m.short[f, w] for f in m.F for w in m.W)
        return salary + penalty

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Constraints ----

    # Trainees in week w = those who started in w and w-1 (a 2-week program).
    def trainee_flow_rule(m, w):
        prev = w - 1
        if prev in m.W:
            return m.t[w] == m.start[w] + m.start[prev]
        return m.t[w] == m.start[w]

    m.trainee_flow = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=trainee_flow_rule)

    # A skilled worker trains at most 3 new workers (in the 2-week block).
    def train_cap_rule(m, w):
        return m.start[w] <= d["train_cap"] * m.s[w]

    m.train_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=train_cap_rule)

    # Total new workers trained by end of week 8 equals 50.
    def total_new_rule(m):
        return sum(m.start[w] for w in m.W) == d["new_workers_total"]

    m.total_new = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_new_rule)

    # Trained-new workers available in week w: started at least 2 weeks earlier.
    def trained_rule(m, w):
        return m.n[w] == sum(m.start[u] for u in m.W if u <= w - d["train_weeks"])

    m.trained = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=trained_rule)

    # Overtime workers are drawn from the skilled pool.
    def overtime_pool_rule(m, w):
        return m.ot[w] <= m.s[w]

    m.overtime_pool = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=overtime_pool_rule)

    # Production capacity: total worker-hours available each week.
    # Normal workers (skilled + trained-new, excluding those on overtime) work 40 h;
    # overtime workers work 60 h => 40*(s+n) + 20*ot.
    def capacity_rule(m, w):
        hours = (d["normal_hours"] * (m.s[w] + m.n[w])
                 + (d["overtime_hours"] - d["normal_hours"]) * m.ot[w])
        return m.x["I", w] / rate["I"] + m.x["II", w] / rate["II"] <= hours

    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Demand / delivery: production plus shortfall must meet demand each week.
    def demand_rule(m, f, w):
        return m.x[f, w] + m.short[f, w] >= demand[f][w - 1]

    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.F, m.W, rule=demand_rule)

    return m

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "weeks": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8],
    "foods": ["I", "II"],
    # production rate kg per hour per (skilled) worker
    "rate": {"I": 10.0, "II": 6.0},
    # weekly demand (kg) per food per week
    "demand": {
        "I":  {1: 10.0, 2: 10.0, 3: 12.0, 4: 12.0, 5: 16.0, 6: 16.0, 7: 20.0, 8: 20.0},
        "II": {1:  6.0, 2:  7.2, 3:  8.4, 4: 10.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 12.0, 7: 12.0, 8: 12.0},
    },
    "skilled_now": 50,
    "hours_normal": 40,        # hours/week normal shift
    "hours_overtime": 60,      # hours/week overtime shift
    "wage_skilled": 360.0,     # yuan/week normal skilled
    "wage_overtime": 540.0,    # yuan/week overtime skilled
    "wage_trainee": 120.0,     # yuan/week during training
    "wage_finished": 240.0,    # yuan/week after training
    "train_per_worker": 3,     # max new workers trained per skilled worker per 2-week period
    "train_weeks": 2,          # training duration in weeks
    "new_workers_target": 50,  # train 50 new workers by end of week 8
    "penalty": {"I": 0.50, "II": 0.60},  # yuan/kg compensation
    "bigM": 10000.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    weeks = d["weeks"]
    foods = d["foods"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.weeks = pyo.Set(initialize=weeks)
    model.foods = pyo.Set(initialize=foods)

    # Decision variables ---------------------------------------------------
    # new trainees in training this week
    model.n = pyo.Var(model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # trainees that finished training and now work as skilled
    model.f = pyo.Var(model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # workers on overtime shift (60 h)
    model.o = pyo.Var(model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # skilled workers assigned to training duties
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # number of new trainees started each week
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # production (kg)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.foods, model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # undelivered / backordered quantity (kg)
    model.b = pyo.Var(model.foods, model.weeks, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective ------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        cost = 0
        for t in m.weeks:
            # normal skilled wage (all skilled except those on overtime pay premium separately)
            cost += d["wage_skilled"] * d["skilled_now"]
            # finished trainees wage
            cost += d["wage_finished"] * m.f[t]
            # trainees in training wage
            cost += d["wage_trainee"] * m.n[t]
            # overtime premium: overtime workers get 540 instead of 360 already paid
            cost += (d["wage_overtime"] - d["wage_skilled"]) * m.o[t]
            # compensation for undelivered food
            for p in m.foods:
                cost += d["penalty"][p] * m.b[p, t]
        return cost

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraints ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Production capacity: available labour-hours * rate = production
    # Skilled workers (excluding trainers, excluding overtime) work normal hours;
    # finished trainees work normal hours; overtime workers give extra hours.
    def prod_cap_rule(m, p, t):
        # normal-hours workers: skilled minus trainers + finished trainees
        normal_workers = d["skilled_now"] - m.u[t] + m.f[t]
        normal_hours = normal_workers * d["hours_normal"]
        # overtime workers contribute extra hours beyond normal
        overtime_extra = m.o[t] * (d["hours_overtime"] - d["hours_normal"])
        # total available hours = normal_hours + overtime_extra  (>=0)
        available_hours = normal_hours + overtime_extra
        return m.x[p, t] <= d["rate"][p] * available_hours

    model.prod_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.foods, model.weeks, rule=prod_cap_rule)

    # Trainer capacity: each skilled worker trains at most 3 new workers over 2 weeks
    def trainer_cap_rule(m, t):
        # trainers active in weeks t-1 and t can each handle train_per_worker
        prev = t - 1
        trainers = m.u[t]
        if prev in weeks:
            trainers = m.u[t] + m.u[prev]
        return d["train_weeks"] * m.y[t] <= d["train_per_worker"] * trainers

    model.trainer_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.weeks, rule=trainer_cap_rule)

    # Training flow: trainees started at week t enter training next 2 weeks
    def training_flow_rule(m, t):
        # n[t] = number in training this week = y[t] (start)  (2-week training)
        return m.n[t] == m.y[t]

    model.training_flow = pyo.Constraint(model.weeks, rule=training_flow_rule)

    # Finished trainees: those who started 2 weeks ago become available
    def finished_rule(m, t):
        start = t - d["train_weeks"]
        if start in weeks:
            return m.f[t] == m.y[start]
        return m.f[t] == 0

    model.finished = pyo.Constraint(model.weeks, rule=finished_rule)

    # Total new workers trained by end of week 8
    def total_new_rule(m):
        return sum(m.y[t] for t in m.weeks) >= d["new_workers_target"]

    model.total_new = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_new_rule)

    # Demand satisfaction with backorders
    def demand_rule(m, p, t):
        prev = t - 1
        backlog = m.b[p, prev] if prev in weeks else 0
        return m.x[p, t] + backlog - m.b[p, t] == d["demand"][p][t]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.foods, model.weeks, rule=demand_rule)

    return model
